**Work Instruction**

**Inspection Route**

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width:5.90556in;height:2.62361in" />

**OBJECTIVE**

This Work Instruction exists to ensure that inspection routes are properly adjusted and performed according to a standard established and agreed upon among managers.

The technician or coordinator who performs a route outside the pre-established standard is fully responsible for it.

It is normal for changes to be made according to the needs of the client visited; however, they must be reported and the possibility of revising the WI and adapting the specific procedure for that operation must be assessed.

# 1- Route Definition
## a) Definition of the Routes to Be Performed
It is the contract coordinator’s responsibility to establish the route scope to be performed by employees, stipulated as daily, every 3 days, weekly, or biweekly.

- Preparation based on equipment criticality. Each client has its own criticality criteria and terminology; in any case, we will use the terminology A+ - A - B - C.

> Add the distance between points and the unit’s terrain relief to plan the inspection route.

1.  Define a route calendar and schedule employees according to the timetable.

<!-- -->

1)  Take into consideration emergencies at the units, which will be considered in day-to-day activities, as well as holidays observed by the unit.

2)  Evaluate operational demands for scheduled services as well as scheduled and unscheduled shutdowns.

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width:5.90556in;height:3.38056in" />

# 2- Inspection Route Path
## a) Division of Priorities + Criticalities
A division will be made among asset criticalities, where time and priority must be allocated to A+ criticality equipment, that is, the equipment classified as A+ according to our priority characteristics.

## b) A+ Priority Technician
The technician assigned to inspect A+ critical equipment must, according to topic 1, perform the inspection of the equipment and, after completing the activities on A+ critical equipment, proceed with the other equipment of different criticalities.

## c) A / B / C Priority Technician
The technician assigned to A / B / C equipment must perform the inspection routes following the subsequent topics.

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width:5.90556in;height:3.36111in" />

# 3- Inspection Route
## a) Authorization to Enter the Area
The technician, together with the operational area and Chesterton and unit coordination teams, will define the best way to obtain work permit authorization in order to perform the inspection route. Check the flowchart in the SOP.

## b) Equipment Inspection
According to the defined predictive inspection **WI**, follow the inspection standards.

## c) Opening an SGA Form
After inspecting the asset, we will identify whether adjustments are necessary on the equipment and whether we need to inform the client. To open the form, we will use SGA and indicate everything being inspected on the equipment, including equipment under observation.

## d) Inspection Analysis
Upon completion of the inspection, an inspection analysis is required, in which the client and our route system will be informed whether or not a problem was found in the equipment.

If no problem is found, the inspection will be completed.

If a problem is found, it will be directed to another procedure.

## e) Notification
Notify the client of the problem found.

The notification depends on each unit and is directly related to how the client proposes managing problem information. It will usually be done in the following ways.

E-mail

ERP (work order opening system)

1.  A maintenance notification number will be generated.

2.  A maintenance notification will be opened in the SGA Form.

The notification informed by the system will be added to the SGA system. The notification number will be entered at the time or later, as soon as it is passed on to our management, and the client’s notification number will be added to the notification opened in the system.

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width:5.90556in;height:3.33542in" />

# 4) Predictive Inspection on Routes

**The Chesterton inspection route begins with the correct identification of the equipment and is divided into numerous inspection stages.**

1.  Check the sealing component.

<!-- -->

1)  Mechanical seal:

> Check the mechanical seal for overall integrity, as well as visible parts such as the gland and metal parts. Observe small leaks as well as the leakage level, dripping, spray pattern, full seal opening, and check leaks from the internal or external seal.

2)  Packing:

> Check the adjustments to be performed, whether there is a need to adjust the packing gland and the amount of packing leakage. Check the condition of the packing gland as well as the sleeve, if necessary.

2.  Check the Sealing Plan

<!-- -->

1)  Check the sealing plan, inspect all tubes or hoses and sensors, as well as heat exchangers, Intelliflow, flowmeters, flow or pressure regulators, and, if necessary, inspect the sealing pots and fluid level.

<!-- -->

3.  Inspect the hydrodynamic peripherals of the assembly.

<!-- -->

1)  Analyze all hydrodynamic peripherals of the assembly, valves, and pressure indicators for both discharge and suction. Evaluate expansion joints or pipe support fastenings, and evaluate pipe alignment with the pumps, both suction and discharge.

<!-- -->

4.  Check Assembly Fastening

<!-- -->

1)  The rotating assembly consists of a motor and pump; therefore, it is fastened with bolts to a fixed base supported directly on concrete or grout, or on a metal base. In these aspects, the evaluation must be carried out on the following items:

<!-- -->

1.  Check the pump structure, integrity, and pump body, checking for cracks and corrosion.

2.  Suction bolts.

3.  Discharge bolts.

4.  Pump base bolts.

5.  Volute bolts.

6.  Check the pump fluid leveler cup, or sight glass.

7.  Motor base bolts.

8.  Check the quantity of shims installed under the motor foot; excessive shims on the motor and pump may cause soft foot.

9.  For bases mounted on Vibra-Stop, check the Vibra-Stop supports.

10. For fixed concrete bases, check the integrity of the base and whether there are cracks or shims on the metal bases.

11. Check the coupling and its fastening.

<!-- -->

5.  Collect Vibration

<!-- -->

1)  Collect vibration at the five points of the centrifugal pump.

2)  Vibration collection provides better failure predictability performance, indicating whether the equipment may fail prematurely.

3)  The vibration collection points on the pump are HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, and AXIAL.

4)  The highest value will be reported in Comments / Recommendations (Client Equipment).

5)  Vibration values are determined according to certain variables:

<!-- -->

1.  Equipment history

2.  Physical structure of the equipment (vertical/horizontal)

3.  Design structure

4.  Reference to the ISO table.

> <img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width:5.90556in;height:3.35in" />

# G) Service Performed
We must identify the equipment on which the service will be performed and start the entire process:

1.  Analyze the activity to be performed.

2.  Follow the flowchart to perform the SAFE ACTIVITY with work permit authorization.

3.  **Mechanical Seal Replacement: follow the WI**

4.  **Packing Replacement: follow the WI**

5.  After completing the related service activity, it is necessary to indicate in the SGA Form the service that was performed.

6.  In the SGA field for the reason for packing replacement, it is necessary to consult the SAP field.

7.  Check the SOP flowchart to identify the actions in case of “Open Notification” or “No Notification.”

8.  Open the service order in SGA:

At this stage, identifying the reason for the intervention is extremely important, as it will characterize the type of failure and whether it will be included in the MTBF calculation.

9.  When there is no mechanical seal replacement or packing replacement, there is no need to open a service order in SGA.

10. For seal and packing replacement, opening a notification in SGA is mandatory.

11. The equipment TAG will be identified in SGA.

12. If the TAG does not exist, equipment will be created in SGA as described in the SGA **WI**.

13. Afterward, a service order will be created in SGA.

14. To prepare a service order, consult the **WI**.

15. A failure analysis will be created, linked to the contract stock transaction:

This type of control is mandatory and is one of the golden rules, because through this control we will be able to count seal failures, generate metrics, and establish better-defined criteria.

For packing, this will also be necessary because we will be better informed about the quantity used and the stipulated size.
